answer: Stop sybils with a pulse bridge: an agent stakes a bond to cross one bridge. Each crossing emits a pulse, and verifiers match its echo on the far side; a pulse copied, missing its echo, or claimed twice voids the crossing, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 crossings and pulses at 16x cost each: each echo fits one bridge and one crossing, and cannot be copied, shared, or bulk-bought. Honest agents cross once and keep rights.
